## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 52 (*Aṅgulipatodaka*) is a disciplinary rule in the *Vinaya Piṭaka* governing the conduct of Buddhist monks [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a monk who tickles another monk commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) and must confess it [SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship and translations, the text has been rendered into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary literature passages retrieved in the research dossier discuss this rule; instead, they address the homonymous Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 52 concerning verbal abuse of monks.

According to SuttaCentral, full parallels to the rule are attested widely across Buddhist Vinaya traditions, including the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Pc 52) and *Parivāra*, as well as the Vinayas and Prātimokṣas of the Sarvāstivāda (Pc 63), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Pc 63), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 54), Mahāsaṅghika (Pc 67), Dharmaguptaka (Pc 53), Lokottaravāda (Pc 67), and Kāśyapīya lineages in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. A counterpart rule for nuns also exists in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pācittiya 133) and across the corresponding non-Theravāda nuns' codes [SuttaCentral]. In automated text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus records 433 internal Pali matches across 71 texts, showing substantial formulaic overlap with other Vinaya rules such as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pārājika 5 (especially §2.2.3–2.2.16), Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 2, several subsequent Pācittiya rules (such as Pc 2, Pc 13, and Pc 72–78), and the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches meeting its threshold [DharmaNexus].
